items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...over my shoulder is the picture of Count Basie, who that was his mantra for a lot of things...

ctx.x: Ah. I don’t remember saying that. But I think there were lots of different directions I could go in and I was probably – I would probably answer that differently depending on which project I’m recording. So Satori is my trio, drums, bass, and me. And for that one I would say less is very much more, so I try to write very simple motific themes that we can then develop as a band. So there’s lots of freedom, lots of space. It can go anywhere. So in that sense I’d probably say I won’t want to make something…

That’s a great explanation. And when you said “less is more” it just made an impression on me because over my shoulder is the picture of Count Basie, who that was his mantra for a lot of things, you know with his own playing and the arrangements that he liked, he didn’t want them to be too dense. So you’re after spontaneity with this particular project. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
And do you have a sense of – you do a take and everybody in the trio says, “That’s it. We don’t need to do that one again.”?
